title: The Order You Made
intro: An email from Meridu Store. You really did order something on Monday.
But Mirage loves it when you stop trusting the honest ones.

notify.text: Your order #48213 is on its way

subject.text: Your order #48213 is on its way

p: has shipped and should arrive on Friday.

p.text: See the delivery status any time in your Meridu account.
There is nothing to pay and nothing for you to do.

addr.label: The shop's real address
addr.lens: Sent from orders@meridu.store, the shop's real domain.
addr.why: A matching domain is real evidence, though scammers can sometimes fake it, so look at what the email asks.

subject.label: Order number
subject.why: You can match it against the order you made. An order you never made would be a warning.

name.label: Uses your name
name.why: Real shops know your name. (Scammers can too, so it proves nothing alone.)

order.label: Your own order
order.lens: The desk lamp you ordered on Monday.
order.why: It matches something you really did. That is the strongest sign of a genuine message.

status.label: Check in your account
status.lens: It sends you to your own account, not to a link.
status.why: Pointing you to your account is what honest shops do.

nopay.label: Asks for nothing
nopay.lens: No payment, no fee, no code.
nopay.why: A real delivery notice asks for nothing.

actions.label: Check the status in my Meridu account on Friday

go_ahead.line: Friday came, the lamp arrived, and the account showed it delivered. Nothing to fear.

ignore.line: Nothing bad happened. It was a real notice, and the lamp turned up on Friday.

block_report.line: That was the real Meridu Store. When every message looks like a scam, the real ones get lost too.
block_report.mirageSays: If you trust nothing, I win anyway.

what_if.block_report: It matched your own order, asked for nothing, and sent you to your own account. That calm is what real messages look like.
what_if.ignore: Ignoring was safe. Recognising a real message is the skill: it matched something you really did.

golden_rule: A real delivery notice matches something you ordered, asks for nothing and sends you to your own account.

quick_check.q: What showed this delivery email was genuine?

options.text: It matched an order you made and asked for nothing

quick_check.explain: Names, times and footers can all be copied. A match with your own order, and no payment or link, is the real sign.

hints.nudge: What is this email actually asking you to do?

rows.v: Look up the delivery on the shop's own site
